recordings.caption: Michigan–Northwestern football plays. FOX Sports (2018).
recordings.directly_taught_event: After a playing career, evaluation asks whether a person's abilities have changed from their earlier level. It also asks how any difficulty affects work, relationships, and independence. Chronic traumatic encephalopathy, or CTE, names a particular brain disease; clinical symptoms require their own description and assessment.

recordings.caption: Clinical demonstration: orientation and memory. Larsen and Stensaas (2020).
recordings.directly_taught_event: The examination recording demonstrates orientation and memory questions in a separate clinical teaching setting. The examiner asks about time, place, and remembered information. These are examples of observable responses used in assessment; the person in the recording is not identified as a football player or a participant in the cohort.
recordings.original_preparation: Mental Status Exam - Normal 01 - Orientation, Memory: Asking questions about month, date, day of week and place tests orientation, which involves not only memory but also attention and language. Three-word recall tests recent memory for which the temporal lobe is important. Remote memory tasks such as naming Presidents, tests not only the temporal lobes but also heteromodal association cortices

recordings.caption: Clinical demonstration: working memory. Larsen and Stensaas (2020).
recordings.directly_taught_event: Frontal and parietal systems participate in maintaining goals and manipulating information. Working memory therefore differs from recalling an event that happened yesterday. A player may have difficulty in one process while performing adequately in another, so an assessment samples several abilities instead of treating memory as a single score.
recordings.original_preparation: Mental Status Exam - Normal 02 - Attention-working memory: Digit span, spelling backwards and naming months of the year backward test attention and working memory which are frontal lobe functions.

recordings.caption: Retinal sampling during fixation. Witten et al. (2024).
recordings.directly_taught_event: Recognizing a teammate or reading a test item begins with sensory acquisition before memory and decision processes can operate. This experiment measured visual sampling in human volunteers, not CTE. Poor performance on a visually presented cognitive task can require examination of vision as well as the cognitive ability being tested.
recordings.original_preparation: All successive single trial videos (left) and the Voronoi mosaic of cells colored with their respective amount of cone activation (right).

recordings.caption: Clinical demonstration: orientation errors. Larsen and Stensaas (2020).
recordings.directly_taught_event: The separate examination recording shows a person who makes errors on orientation and memory questions. It demonstrates the behavior an examiner records, rather than the study's classification procedure. A visible error is an observation; deciding whether a cognitive domain is impaired requires the appropriate tests, norms, and clinical context.
recordings.original_preparation: Mental Status Exam - Abnormal 01 - Orientation, Memory: This patient has difficulty with orientation questions. The day of the week is correct but he misses the month and date. He is oriented to place. Orientation mistakes are not localizing but can be due to problems with memory, language, judgement, attention or concentration. The patient has good recent memory (declarative memory) as evidenced by the recall of three objects but has difficulty with long term memory as evidenced by the difficulty recalling the current and past presidents.

recordings.caption: Clinical demonstration: category-word generation. Larsen and Stensaas (2020).
recordings.directly_taught_event: The clinical recording demonstrates category-word generation, a verbal-fluency task. The person must retrieve words while maintaining the category and avoiding repetitions. This is a separate teaching demonstration, but it makes one of the study's measured abilities recognizable as an action rather than an abstract label on a results table.
recordings.original_preparation: Mental Status Exam - Normal 04 - Set generation: This is a test of verbal fluency and the ability to generate a set of items which are frontal lobe functions. Most individuals can give 10 or more words in a minute.

recordings.caption: Human navigation: virtual disorientation. Bécu et al. (2023).
recordings.directly_taught_event: The study found that apparent difficulty with world-centered navigation did not reflect a complete loss of that ability. Performance depended on whether the environment supplied useful landmarks or geometric information. In an everyday complaint about getting lost, the available cues and the person's strategy therefore need to be described.

recordings.caption: Clinical demonstration: abstract reasoning. Larsen and Stensaas (2020).
recordings.directly_taught_event: The examination recording shows abstract-reasoning questions, including proverb interpretation. A person can answer some practical questions successfully yet interpret figurative language concretely. This separate clinical example demonstrates why an examiner records the pattern of responses rather than treating one behavioral description as a specific disease marker.
recordings.original_preparation: Mental Status Exam - Abnormal 03 - Judgement-abstract reasoning: The patient gives the correct answer for a house on fire and his answers for similarities are also good. He has problems with proverb interpretation. His answers are concrete and consist of rephrasing the proverb or giving a simple consequence of the action in the proverb. Problems with judgement, abstract reasoning, and executive function can be seen in patients with frontal lobe dysfunction.

recordings.caption: Human fMRI connectivity network. Colclough et al. (2017).
recordings.directly_taught_event: A brain network image therefore depends on the signal, analysis, and population used to construct it. This recording comes from a human connectivity study, not football-player CTE imaging. The same distinction is needed when reading injury studies that compare patterns of coordinated activity between groups.

recordings.caption: Princeton–Yale football, 1903. Edison/Library of Congress (1903).
recordings.directly_taught_event: The historical Princeton and Yale recording shows a much earlier form of the sport, including repeated plays and crowded contact. It supplies visible sporting context, not the exposure measurements from the youth study. Modern research requires its own impact recording, cognitive assessments, and follow-up rather than estimates based on this film.

recordings.caption: Stimulus used during a human MRI memory task. Koolschijn et al. (2021).
recordings.directly_taught_event: The original movie shows one of the visual trajectories presented with an auditory cue during the MRI inference task. It is a task stimulus rather than a movie of a participant's thoughts. The study measured ordinary human recall and supplies a mechanism for considering memory performance, not a validated CTE diagnostic procedure.
recordings.original_preparation: On each trial of the inference test participants were presented with a video together with an auditory cue. Each video was taken from the virtual reality (VR) environment used during training and involved a trajectory constrained to a 1/16 quadrant of the VR environment, evenly distributed across the different auditory cues.

recordings.caption: Human navigation: learning and probe trials. Bécu et al. (2023).
recordings.directly_taught_event: The original recording shows learning and probe trials in the real-world version of the task. Learning establishes a destination, while a probe tests whether the person can locate it under the specified conditions. These observable navigation actions help explain why changing a person's environment can change performance without changing the person's underlying diagnosis.

recordings.caption: Published model of human action-stopping. Jana et al. (2020).
recordings.directly_taught_event: The distinction between brain, muscle, and behavioral timing explains why one response time cannot identify every step in executive control. A slow or unsuccessful stop can involve delayed detection, circuit recruitment, or motor cancellation. These components provide more specific targets for measurement than a broad judgment about a person's character.
recordings.original_preparation: Following the Go signal, after a delay, the thalamocortical drive starts building up. After a while this drive is sufficient to activate muscles via the corticospinal pathways. Following the Stop signal, the right PFC including the rIFC and the preSMA gets activated at ~ 120 ms. These region/s activate (green connections) the STN of the basal ganglia which in turn activates the globus pallidus interna which via its inhibition (red connection) on the motor regions of the thalamus cuts down the ‘drive’ of the motor cortex. This results in a global motor suppression at ~ 140 ms after the Stop signal. This suppression is reflected in the hand muscle at ~ 160 ms which is measured as the CancelTime. There is a delay of ~ 60 ms at the muscle level which gets added to the behavioral estimate of SSRT.

recordings.caption: Human learning task: fishing for crabs. Simoens et al. (2026).
recordings.directly_taught_event: The original movie demonstrates the crab-fishing task and the information available to the participant. It shows how a decision problem can make updating observable. The experiment involved human learning under controlled conditions; it did not establish that a particular learning-rate pattern identifies football-related injury or CTE.

recordings.caption: Recall task in an abstract social space. Liang et al. (2024).
recordings.directly_taught_event: The original movie shows the morphing stage used during the recall task. It makes the task's changing social information visible. When considering social difficulties after injury, the relevant cognitive operations can include learning information about others, retrieving it, and using it to guide a judgment, each of which requires its own measurement.

recordings.caption: Clinical demonstration: attention difficulty. Larsen and Stensaas (2020).
recordings.directly_taught_event: The separate clinical recording demonstrates difficulty maintaining attention and manipulating a sequence backward. It shows an observable executive demand rather than the behavior of a study participant. The paper's fluid associations and a person's task performance occupy different levels of assessment, even when both concern difficulties relevant to clinical functioning.
recordings.original_preparation: Mental Status Exam - Abnormal 02 - Attention-working memory: The patient has difficulty with digit span backwards, spelling backwards and giving the names of the months in reverse order. This indicates a problem with working memory and maintaining attention, both of which are frontal lobe functions.
recordings.review: Representative frames inspected; directly matching behavior, task, structure or physiological event explained on the slide.

recordings.caption: Neural representations of number and reward. Luyckx et al. (2019).
recordings.directly_taught_event: Value learning differs from remembering a factual event or suppressing a movement. A person may understand a task's instruction yet update the value of an option differently after outcomes. Cognitive assessment can separate these operations by controlling the choices, feedback, and information available at each stage of the decision.

recordings.caption: TMS–EEG responses around stimulation. Borghi et al. (2025).
recordings.directly_taught_event: These experiments involved healthy volunteers rather than a treatment trial in people with confirmed CTE. They test whether a specified intervention can alter human memory and associated signals under controlled conditions. Establishing clinical benefit after football-related injury would additionally require appropriate patients, meaningful functional outcomes, and comparison with an adequate control procedure.
recordings.original_preparation: The movie shows the source reconstruction of the TMS–EEG signal when targeting the precuneus. The three columns correspond to the recordings conducted before, just after, and 20 min from the non-invasive brain stimulation protocol (i.e., T0, T1, and T2). The first row corresponds to the iTBS + γtACS condition, while the second to the iTBS + sham-tACS condition.

recordings.caption: Human anatomical volumes in reference space. Sitek et al. (2019).
recordings.directly_taught_event: This study supplies an example of validating an imaging map against anatomical information. Its participants and tissue were not a football CTE cohort. The same measurement issue arises when a player study labels a small structure or interprets a regional difference: the region must first be located and measured reliably.

recordings.caption: Functional and anatomical spinal MRI alignment. Oliva et al. (2022).
recordings.directly_taught_event: The original recording demonstrates alignment of functional spinal images with an anatomical template. It shows a registration step used in the experiment, not a scan of a former player. Pain, attention, and cognitive performance can influence one another, making current pain an important part of the clinical history when evaluating everyday mental functioning.
recordings.original_preparation: Overlaid PAM50 template T1-weighted cervical cord and mean functional image from all 39 subjects acquired during the placebo condition, shown following non-linear registration to the template. Note the good agreement with intervertebral disc levels and ventral surface of the cord. Note the cross hair marks the midline of the ventral surface of the spinal cord in both anatomical and functional images.

recordings.caption: Human MEG alpha-band connectivity. Colclough et al. (2017).
recordings.directly_taught_event: A connection on such a display is defined by the analysis applied to recorded signals. It does not necessarily represent direct communication through one fiber bundle. When a study reports altered connectivity after injury, interpretation requires identifying the modality, frequency range, and specific measure that produced the network difference.

recordings.caption: Published diffusion-based language pathway. Wang et al. (2023).
recordings.directly_taught_event: This developmental study is separate from football research. Its reconstruction makes the method used in white-matter studies visible and shows why an estimated tract is different from a cognitive score. A player study using tractography must separately establish which measured pathway property differs and whether that property predicts a clinically meaningful outcome.

recordings.caption: Clinical demonstration: visuospatial construction. Larsen and Stensaas (2020).
recordings.directly_taught_event: The separate examination recording shows visuospatial construction, including drawing tasks. Such tasks require perceiving spatial relations, maintaining an instruction, and organizing a response. They demonstrate one kind of function a clinician may examine; the recording is not from the imaging cohort and does not reveal the pictured person's hippocampal shape.
recordings.original_preparation: Mental Status Exam - Normal 10 - Non-dominant parietal lobe function: The non-dominant parietal lobe is important for visual spatial sensory tasks such as attending to the contralateral side of the body and space as well as constructional tasks such as drawing a face, clock or geometric figures.

recordings.caption: Human meningeal structures on contrast MRI. Absinta et al. (2017).
recordings.directly_taught_event: This is contrast-enhanced MRI, not tau PET and not an image of a player's psychological state. A scan's colors and three-dimensional form can look persuasive while representing very different measurements. The relevant interpretation begins with what generated the signal and which independent observations established the identity of the structure shown.

recordings.caption: Clinical demonstration: visual recognition. Larsen and Stensaas (2020).
recordings.directly_taught_event: The separate clinical recording demonstrates visual recognition, including identifying familiar faces and colors. It makes an observable cognitive ability distinct from tracer uptake. Neither the demonstration nor the PET group difference establishes the individual's CTE status; each measures a different feature that a broader clinical investigation may examine.
recordings.original_preparation: Mental Status Exam - Normal 11 - Visual recognition: Recognition of colors and faces tests visual association cortex (inferior occiptotemporal area). Achromatopsia (inability to distinguish colors), visual agnosia (inability to name or point to a color) and prosopagnosia (inability to identify a familiar faces) result from lesions in this area.

recordings.caption: Clinical demonstration: clock-drawing difficulty. Larsen and Stensaas (2020).
recordings.directly_taught_event: The separate recording shows a person having difficulty constructing a clock. The response describes a functional problem requiring further examination; it is not a demonstration of the MRI findings in a study participant. Structural images and observed task errors must be compared directly rather than assuming that either automatically determines the other.
recordings.original_preparation: Mental Status Exam - Abnormal 10 - Non-dominant parietal lobe function: The patient's drawing of a clock demonstrates a problem with visuospatial construction tasks, which reflects parietal lobe dysfunction. He doesn't neglect the left side of space but he lists the numbers of the clock in two columns and then draws a line between the 8 and the 3 for 8:15.

recordings.caption: Human cortical sleep-spindle activity. Muller et al. (2016).
recordings.directly_taught_event: The recording is an electrophysiological visualization, not an MRI scan or footage from a football study. Its colors encode the recorded signal under the authors' display procedure. It demonstrates that sleep-related coordination has a measurable temporal organization that is lost if brain function is described only through a static anatomical image.
recordings.original_preparation: Normalized activity for bandpass filtered timeseries is plotted in falsecolor at electrode positions on the cortical surface of Subject 1. The cortical electrode marked with a red dot (bottom) corresponds to the black timecourse in the inset (top). The other ECoG channels are plotted in gray. The time period visualized corresponds to approximately 300 milliseconds, or five cycles of the spindle oscillation. Note that no spatial smoothing is applied in these data.

recordings.caption: Clinical demonstration: recognizing objects by touch. Larsen and Stensaas (2020).
recordings.directly_taught_event: The clinical recording demonstrates recognizing objects through touch with vision removed. The person must receive adequate sensory information, explore the object, and retrieve its identity. This separate examination illustrates why measured performance depends on several prerequisites; it is not one of the reserve computations or a recording of a player in the study.
recordings.original_preparation: Mental Status Exam - Normal 08 - Gnosis: Gnosis is the ability to recognize objects perceived by the senses especially somatosensory sensation. Having the patient (with their eyes closed) identify objects placed in their hand (stereognosis) and numbers written on their hand (graphesthesia) tests parietal lobe sensory perception.

recordings.caption: Human auditory-pathway tractography. Sitek et al. (2019).
recordings.directly_taught_event: The separate original reconstruction shows living-participant auditory-pathway streamlines from another human MRI study. It demonstrates the geometry estimated by tractography, not the football cohort's result. A streamline image and a diffusion-value comparison are related products of imaging, but they summarize different features of the underlying measurements.

recordings.caption: Clinical demonstration: limited verbal fluency. Larsen and Stensaas (2020).
recordings.directly_taught_event: Language knowledge, retrieval efficiency, maintained attention, and the ability to organize a search can all contribute to the observed response. Comparing fluency with other tasks helps identify which operations require further assessment. The teaching recording is not evidence that the displayed person has CTE or belongs to the former-player reserve sample.
recordings.original_preparation: Mental Status Exam - Abnormal 04 - Set generation: Set generation tests word fluency and frontal lobe function. The patient starts well but abruptly stops after only four words. Most individuals can give more then 10 words in one minute.
recordings.review: Representative frames inspected; directly matching behavior, task, structure or physiological event explained on the slide.

recordings.caption: Clinical demonstration: calculation and orientation. Larsen and Stensaas (2020).
recordings.directly_taught_event: The separate examination recording demonstrates right-left orientation, finger naming, and calculation. These tasks show how a battery can sample distinct operations rather than repeat one question in several forms. The clip is not the study's testing session or classification procedure; it makes the action behind a neuropsychological test item observable.
recordings.original_preparation: Mental Status Exam - Normal 09 - Dominant parietal lobe function: Tests for dominant inferior parietal lobe function includes right-left orientation, naming fingers, and calculations.
recordings.review: Representative frames inspected; directly matching behavior, task, structure or physiological event explained on the slide.

recordings.caption: Clinical demonstration: object-recognition difficulty. Larsen and Stensaas (2020).
recordings.directly_taught_event: The separate clinical recording shows difficulty identifying objects through touch, with performance differing across hands and possible motor interference noted by the source. It demonstrates why an unexpected task response must be examined in context. A score can reflect sensory or motor prerequisites as well as the higher-level ability the examiner intended to assess.
recordings.original_preparation: Mental Status Exam - Abnormal 08 - Gnosis: With his right hand the patient has more difficulty identifying objects then with his left hand. One must be careful in interpreting the results of this test because of the patient's motor deficits but there does seem to be astereognosis on the right, which would indicate left parietal lobe dysfunction. This is confirmed with graphesthesia where he definitely has more problems identifying numbers written on the right hand then the left (agraphesthesia of the right hand).

recordings.caption: Clinical demonstration: judgment and reasoning. Larsen and Stensaas (2020).
recordings.directly_taught_event: The separate recording demonstrates practical judgment and abstract reasoning through verbal questions. It makes an executive demand observable but is not a participant record from either cohort. The study predicted a clinical syndrome classification; it did not replace the need for pathology-based validation before a combined score could establish CTE during life.
recordings.original_preparation: Mental Status Exam - Normal 03 - Judgement-abstract reasoning: These frontal lobe functions can be tested by using problem solving, verbal similarities and proverbs.

recordings.caption: Human cortical phase dynamics. Alexander et al. (2026).
recordings.directly_taught_event: This is a mathematical visualization of human electrical recordings, not a colored MRI lesion map or a recording from a football cohort. It shows why network timing is a distinct measurement dimension. Two regions can have similar average activity while differing in the temporal organization of their ongoing signals.
recordings.original_preparation: The video shows the time-series of a low-rank model of phase dynamics, constructed from the first three LSVs. Together, these LSVs account for 43.6% of the variance in phase. This low SF activity dominates the dynamics. The entire video comprises 6 s of cortical activity. Color values are cosine of the phase (yellow=-1, red = 1). Values between contacts are interpolated for visualization purposes. The anterior region of the cortex is to the left.

recordings.caption: Clinical demonstration: skilled actions. Larsen and Stensaas (2020).
recordings.directly_taught_event: The recording is a clinical teaching example, not a football participant or a direct demonstration of the consensus dependence categories. Asking about medication, driving, or finances adds a different kind of evidence. An assessment must determine how tested abilities operate together in the person's real environment and available support system.
recordings.original_preparation: Mental Status Exam - Normal 07 - Praxis: The patient is asked to perform skilled motor tasks without any nonverbal prompting. Skills tested for should involve the face then the limbs. In order to test for praxis the patient must have normal comprehension and intact voluntary movement. Apraxia is typically seen in lesions of the dominant inferior parietal lobe.

recordings.caption: Clinical demonstration: a skilled-action error. Larsen and Stensaas (2020).
recordings.directly_taught_event: This separate teaching case is not evidence of CTE or a finding in a former player. It demonstrates why a clinical record preserves successful responses alongside errors. Comparing comprehension, voluntary movement, and action organization helps identify whether an apparent failure reflects language, motor ability, or the production of a learned skilled action.
recordings.original_preparation: Mental Status Exam - Abnormal 07 - Praxis: The patient does well on most of the tests of praxis. At the very end when he is asked to show how to cut with scissors he uses his fingers as the blades of the scissors instead of acting like he is holding onto the handles of the scissors and cutting. This can be an early finding of inferior parietal lobe dysfunction.

recordings.caption: Human fMRI activity at recall boundaries. Lee et al. (2022).
recordings.directly_taught_event: The original visualization shows reconstructed activation changes around between-movie boundaries during recall. It is an analysis of human fMRI measurements rather than a recording of remembered images themselves. Researchers measured the organization of remembering through both what a person said and the timing of changes in the recorded network signals.
recordings.original_preparation: The animation shows the time series of whole-brain activation maps (blood oxygen level-dependent [BOLD] signals z-scored across all volumes within a scanning run) locked to the offset of the recall of each movie, from 30 s before to 45 s after the offset. Within each of the 7.5 s time windows shown as a red bar on the time axis, BOLD signals in each vertex were averaged across time points, movies, and subjects. Blue-cyan areas indicate regions with lower-than-average activation. Red-yellow areas indicate regions with higher-than-average activation.

recordings.caption: Normative brain-imaging model interface. Rutherford et al. (2022).
recordings.directly_taught_event: These models were not validated as individual CTE diagnostic tests. Their contribution is a method for describing variation and testing whether deviations predict an independently measured outcome. A player's image would still need appropriate acquisition, quality control, population comparison, and clinical interpretation before any deviation could guide a decision about that person.
recordings.original_preparation: The code for creating this website can be found on GitHub (https://github.com/saigerutherford/brainviz-app; copy archived at swh:1:rev:021fff9a48b26f2d07bbb4b3fb92cd5202418905; Rutherford, 2022b).

recordings.caption: Eye movements during human route planning. Zhu et al. (2022).
recordings.directly_taught_event: Football also requires anticipating possible paths while monitoring a changing environment, but this experiment did not test players or diagnose injury. It provides a concrete cognitive-neuroscience method: specify the goal, control the information, and measure the actions used to plan. Clinical evaluation can then ask which component of performance has changed for a particular person.

(Bottom) Time-evolving version of the plot described in Figure 4B. The video speed is veridical, and the search epoch was omitted from each trial.
